title: We ask the IC to approve a capped preparation period that buys three decisions, not a company
lead: Conjugates have made muscle reachable for RNA drugs and the market has paid platform prices for that, but the step that decides whether a programme works is still unproven in public. We propose to buy three read-outs before committing to a company.

items.heading: The opportunity
items.body: Antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates turned muscle into a reachable tissue. Novartis paid about USD 12.0 bn for Avidity in February 2026; a second sponsor carries a PDUFA date of 21 January 2027. The modality is proven at tissue entry, not at durable clinical benefit.

items.heading: The gap we would enter
items.body: Public work concentrates on one receptor and a handful of muscle targets. What no one has shown is receptor-dependent productive delivery under free uptake: payload reaching the cytosol of the target cell, measured as such rather than inferred from whole-tissue concentration.

items.heading: Why WuXi
items.body: The group runs the full oligo discovery chain and has delivered 150+ conjugates at five to six weeks' turnaround. What a new company adds is product judgement, patient material, and ownership of rights and primary data.

items.text: What we would buy: a written freedom-to-operate opinion on the receptor antibody and backbone chemistry; a productive-delivery judgement under free uptake with a paired patient-cell arm; and an interpretable conjugate with full payload-distribution characterization.

What we are not deciding today: amounts, valuation, ownership, and the choice between the three company configurations. Thresholds can only be set once the target product profile is fixed, so every figure is marked TBD.

regions.text: Decision requested: approve the preparation period and its five deliverables; release further investment gate by gate on evidence, not on calendar or business milestones.

source: Source: IC Memo v2; Novartis, Avidity, BMS and Dyne disclosures (2025-2026); team analysis
notes: The one page to read if you read nothing else. Lead with the fact that others have de-risked the modality at the tissue-entry level: that is what makes the window real and also what makes it crowded. Our wedge is one layer down. Stress that this is a request for a decision framework, not a cheque.

title: Eight dimensions graded separately on the evidence behind them, with no weighted total
lead: Each dimension is graded by the kind of evidence supporting it - measured, disclosed by a third party, or inferred - and carries its own upgrade read-out and owner. No weighted total is given, because a single score would average away the two dimensions that can stop this investment on their own.
fig_caption: Evidence status by dimension, with the facts that must be settled before any valuation. Total deliberately left blank
points: Rights and delivery are read first
Biology is proven at payload level only
No positive conjugate clinical record yet
Market and team wait on the product profile
table_note: Per-dimension upgrade read-outs, owners and prerequisite facts are listed in full in the memo
limits: Scoring logic: dimensions are graded by evidence type, not by attractiveness. Rights and delivery come first because either can end the case on its own.
If the IC wants an indicative number, the honest version is a pair: high confidence on biology and CMC, low on delivery and rights.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 (§6.1, §6.2, §4.1.7, §2.1); patent workbook; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: The reference template reports a single out-of-100 figure. Here that would hide the fact that two of the eight dimensions rest on inference rather than measurement, so the total stays blank by design - the memo takes the same position. Walk the cards in reading order: rights and delivery, then biology and CMC, then translation, competition, market and team.

title: Four questions this material answers, in the order an investment decision needs them
lead: Each block is worth discussing only if the one above it held. The material stops at the preparation period: the sections on configuration and funding set out options, not a commitment of capital.
fig_caption: The four blocks of this material and what each one settles
points: Why now: the window and the field
How we evaluate: binder, payload, chemistry
Why us: what we already execute
How we build: route, team, money, gates
source: Source: IC Memo v2
notes: Walk the four blocks top to bottom in about a minute. The order is deliberate. Note that the deck deliberately stops at the preparation period.

title: Why now
subtitle: What conjugates made possible, who already occupies the field, and which part of the problem is still open

title: Conjugates moved RNA drugs out of the liver, and the money followed before the biology was finished
lead: Naked and GalNAc oligonucleotides work in the liver and, intrathecally, in the central nervous system. An antibody against a surface receptor extends that reach to muscle, and buyers have paid platform prices for it - while the step that decides efficacy remains unsolved and, in most published work, unmeasured.
fig_caption: Reachable tissues against clinical validation by delivery approach, with the three risks that remain open
points: USD 12.0bn: Novartis for Avidity, Feb 2026
USD 2.3bn: BMS deal, up to five targets
PDUFA 21 Jan 2027 for the first filing
Approved conjugates to date: none
table_note: Deal terms, trial identifiers and filing dates are listed in the memo's competitive annex
limits: Unresolved across the field: endosomal escape efficiency, control and characterization of payload distribution, and on-target toxicity from receptor-mediated uptake.
These three are exactly where conjugation chemistry and delivery measurement decide the outcome, which is where the group's capability sits.
source: Source: Novartis, Avidity, BMS and Dyne disclosures (2025-2026); IC Memo v2
notes: The point of this page is the mismatch between validation and valuation. Buyers have paid platform prices for assets whose central technical problem is still unsolved. That mismatch is the opportunity: the expensive part of the field is the receptor antibody and the clinical asset; the unsolved part is chemistry and measurement.

title: Two companies hold most of the clinical field, and both are now past the readout that defines the ceiling
lead: The crowding is specific: one receptor, one tissue. Of 60 conjugate programmes in our search set, 24 belong to these two sponsors, and the Phase 3 miss in myotonic dystrophy says the hard part is no longer getting in - it is choosing a target and an endpoint where getting in produces benefit.

Tissue entry is not clinical benefit; endpoint choice decides the trial
Del-zota

Splice correction on a surrogate endpoint is the shortest regulatory route
Z-rostudirsen
TfR1 antibody, exon-51 PMO
Accepted with priority review; action date 21 Jan 2027
A second sponsor reaching filing on the same receptor and tissue
Z-basivarsen

Confirmatory Phase 3 dosing since Jul 2026; cohort reads out Q1 2027
The myotonic dystrophy question stays open despite the competitor's miss
Early entrants

source: Source: company disclosures and ClinicalTrials.gov to 2026-11-01; IC Memo v2 (competition)
notes: Three things to draw out. The Phase 3 miss is the most important datum in this deck. Both filings in hand are splice-correction programmes on surrogate endpoints, which is why our first programme is a splice-correction benchmark. And the crowding is specific to one receptor and one tissue, so entry elsewhere is open - but there is no public precedent to lean on either.

title: Human evidence de-risks the skeletal-muscle entry; the window is measured by evidence density and rights
lead: The length of the window cannot be predicted but its closing conditions can be monitored: this round secures rights at the payload-sequence and disease-use layers and turns transfection-free functional data on the first two payloads into our own first readouts.
fig_caption: Nine cards in three bands: risks lowered by human readouts, lowered only at stage or regulatory level, and still to be proven.
points: Nine cards in three bands: lowered by human readouts, lowered only at stage level, and still to be proven.
All three green cards carry human or patient-cell data, but each one's reach is narrow and stated on the card.
The amber band is stage and regulatory fact only; none of it is evidence for any single step of the chain.
Every card below the dashed boundary carries a named gate, so each open risk has an owner this round.
The window has no date: it closes when evidence density or rights maturity moves on five monitored signals.
table_note: Risks lowered by human evidence: reported value with its reach first, judgement after
Closing signals are reviewed quarterly and reported as order of magnitude, never as a rate
limits: Registry reads carry status only and no trial results; the check date is 2026-10-11 and no record was re-verified for this deck.
Human PD for TfR1 into skeletal muscle is company-disclosed with details absent from the material; the reach is skeletal muscle, TfR1 and the classic AOC format only.
Two BLA priority reviews are acceptances, not approvals, and no classic AOC has been approved anywhere in this search set.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 §3.3, §3.4, §3.5, §4.1.7, Appendix D.2/D.4; registry status check 2026-10-11; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: Human readouts have lowered three risks, each with a stated reach: TfR1 delivery into skeletal muscle with measurable PD, nuclear splice correction in patient cells, and randomised benefit for the intrathecal naked ASO route in CNS. Phase 3 status, priority review and the Novartis-Avidity deal lower feasibility and regulatory risk but supply no step-level delivery data, so they sit in the middle column and cannot stand as evidence for any one step of the chain. The right-hand column is what this round pays for: intact molecule in blood, entry into the right cell and productive intracellular payload, each with a named gate. The window itself is defined by evidence density times rights maturity, with no time axis and no weighted score. Cut for space: the full five-signal review cadence and the asset-by-asset gap read.

title: Crowding sits at the delivery entry; the disease layer is read by system and stage against its own denominator
lead: Crowding in AOC is measured in delivery entries and development stages rather than company or disease counts: 7 assets spread across 3 systems while 6 share TfR1, so positioning and the follow-up search list are both generated on the entry and stage axes.
fig_caption: Disease x organ system: asset stage shown by dot colour, delivery modality by dot shape, and three counts that cannot be added.
points: Fourteen organ systems against two asset panels and three counts; dot colour is stage, dot shape is modality.
All five Phase 3 classic AOC assets sit on one row, skeletal muscle; everything else is Phase 1 or absent.
CNS carries the most records and the second-largest patent count but only one classic AOC asset, in Phase 1.
The five counting columns use different units and denominators, so no two of them may be added.
A dash means not captured or not found this round, never 'no competition here'.
table_note: Assets 33, patent publications 60, disease records 94, mechanism-verifiable 31 of 94
A '0' means the search set returns zero by definition; a blank means nothing was looked up
limits: A dash or a blank means not captured or not found this round, which is not the same as 'no competition here'; coverage is representative, not a global picture.
Publication numbers are neither patent families nor granted rights, and column E is broken out for four systems only, covering 25 of 31 records.
'Phase 1' includes Phase 1/2 and 'approved' requires a company announcement corroborated in the registry; CGB1001 is excluded from the figure.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 §3.4, Appendix A, Appendix B, Appendix C.3; ClinicalTrials.gov check 2026-10-11; patent workbook 2026-09-07; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: Every column has its own unit and denominator, so the figure deliberately drops all cross-column totals and any weighted density score. Late-stage activity is concentrated in a single system, skeletal muscle, where all five classic AOC assets sit in Phase 3, while the largest record counts sit in CNS: where the literature is densest is not where assets are most advanced. Blank cells are triaged three ways, as not captured, not found this round, or entry conditions not yet met, and the same entry-by-stage grid generates the follow-up search list. Cut for space: the full five-column statistical-unit table and the per-system record breakdown.

title: Representative companies split into six modality classes; the antibody's increment is answered asset by asset
lead: Competition sits inside the same target and modality and also across alternative ligands and naked-oligonucleotide routes serving the same patients, so the first proposition moves from 'why AOC over naked oligo' to 'why an antibody over an aptamer', measured at the receptor-entry gate.
fig_caption: Evidence tier and modality for 12 named assets and 9 candidate directions across the seven-step chain, under two independent denominators.
points: Twenty-one rows by seven steps: twelve named assets above, nine candidate directions below, separate denominators.
Steps 1 and 4 are empty for every asset: no direct in-material data on blood stability or productive payload.
What evidence exists clusters in step 5, and most of it is company disclosure rather than published detail.
The red frames on del-desiran mark negative results, which is a different state from a missing cell.
Candidate rows carry payload-level evidence only; no AOC has been built for any of the nine directions.
table_note: 26 same-disease assets in six delivery classes (check: 26 = 33 - 7)
Three modality representatives are shown but are not counted in the 13 programmes
limits: Check dates are batched: registry 2026-10-11 and correction items 2026-10-07; the two batches are not merged and no record was re-verified on 2026-11-02.
No classic AOC approval exists in this search set; the two BLA priority reviews, del-zota PDUFA TBD and z-rostudirsen PDUFA 2027-01-21, are acceptances only.
Bulk readouts (tissue homogenate, bulk RNA) do not count toward a gate decision; steps 3 and 4 need cell-level and subcellular resolution before they can be judged.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 §3.3, §3.5, §4.1.5, §10.7, Appendix C.3, Appendix D.2/D.4; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: The competitor table is split into six delivery classes and each asset's configuration is confirmed from three sources, because the comparison is only meaningful inside a class. Not one of the 13 priority programmes has in-material data for intact molecule in blood or for productive intracellular payload, which is the evidential backdrop for treating the step after cell entry as the likeliest failure point. The Denali cell-entry data comes from a MALAT1 tool molecule and is listed apart from the candidate, and HARBOR's failure is not inferred from other programmes on the same platform. Non-antibody ligands set the external benchmark for the antibody increment, and intrathecal naked oligonucleotide is the CNS comparator. Cut for space: the per-asset three-source confirmation log.

title: Rights dependency sits in the receptor-antibody layer; the backbone-chemistry path waits on a supplementary search
lead: The layer NewCo can differentiate on is payload sequence and disease use, while the backbone-chemistry layer needs a supplementary search before a path is chosen. Across the four entry paths the decisive costs are commercial terms, data rebuild, receptor-access rebuild and scarce models.
fig_caption: Core-60 publication numbers by year, plus the two-leaders-and-long-tail split of the 26 merged applicants; grey = pre-merger basis.
points: 29 of the 60 core publications land in 2025-26; nothing in this set before 2018, and the trend is still rising.
Avidity 13 and Dyne 11 hold 40% of the 60; 20 of the other 24 applicants hold a single publication each.
The two leaders concentrate on TfR1 conjugates, linker chemistry and muscle indications - our own entry layer.
Both time-window readings are disclosed side by side: the window is still open, and it is closing.
Dependency sits in the receptor-antibody layer; payload sequence and disease use stay differentiable.
table_note: Three counts kept apart: 135/60 publications, no family counts yet, 2 granted-in-force
Pre-merger 135 basis is reference only and is never added to the 60
limits: Not a freedom-to-operate opinion: changing epitope or sequence is not automatic design-around, process innovation may not solve FTO, and publication does not imply freedom to operate.
A 'Ceased' status on one WO page says nothing about the whole family, and the counts reflect the search set only, not global filing.
2026 is a partial year and publication lags about 18 months, so the last two years are necessarily understated.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 §3.1, §3.2, §4.5, Appendix B; core AOC patent workbook 2026-09-07; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: Filing density is still rising, and the deck discloses both readings of that fact side by side: it makes any FTO conclusion premature, and it also narrows the wait-and-see window. This round does not choose between them. The pre-merger 135-publication basis (Avidity 14, Dyne 12, Arrowhead 5, Denali 5) is shown for reference only and is never added to the 60. Chinese applicants hold 8 of the core 60 across six entities. The first two entry paths fall inside gate work; the last two stay exploratory.

title: How we evaluate
subtitle: Taking a conjugate apart into binder, payload and chemistry, and the evidence a disease candidate must produce

title: AOC splits into binder, payload and conjugation chemistry: three capability lines built separately
lead: Build and commit along three capability lines, not one: this round buys only the configuration-neutral freedom-to-operate & backbone study and the shared productive-delivery study, and reuse is claimed one platform unit at a time, first tested at the platform-transfer gate.
fig_caption: Three modules x three dimensions; each cell gives the existing basis and what must be built, with the commitment owner under each column.
points: Three columns, three dimensions: nine cells, each with an existing basis and a capability still to build.
Everything on the brown line is new work this round; none of it transfers from one module to another.
The commitment bar is green only under the payload line; binder and linker sit at letter of intent, amounts TBD.
Reuse is claimed per platform unit, not per programme: GAA IVS1 and DYSF share one, COL6A1 is the second.
The dashed rights cell is the memo's own layer: thinnest direct evidence, search boundary undefined.
table_note: Classic AOC scope only: direct covalent antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates
Three listed partners; rights boundary and commitment authority stay in the memo
limits: Classic AOC scope only, a direct covalent antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate; antibody-protamine-siRNA complexes, targeted LNP, Centyrin, aptamers, peptides and GalNAc are out of scope.
P=S clearance and the DAR1 versus DAR2 and backbone conclusions hold only inside the published system: female ICR mice, n=4/group, IV dosing, one siRNA chemistry, two loading levels.
Blank cells mean not captured or not found; the figure carries no amounts and no count rankings, and the commitment bars mark ownership only.
notes: We buy and commit along three lines, and each line is owned by a different partner: WuXi AppTec can commit on the payload, while WuXi Biologics and WuXi XDC are at letter-of-intent stage with amounts still TBD. ADC experience runs in reverse on three points: conjugate PK is not predicted by the naked antibody, OAR distribution must be reported in full rather than as a mean, and the backbone-chemistry layer has the thinnest direct evidence and no defined search boundary. Reuse is claimed per platform unit, not per programme, so GAA IVS1 and DYSF share one unit and COL6A1 is held as the second-unit candidate. Cut for space: the three-company rights-boundary table and the detail of commitment authority.

title: Each payload class acts in its own compartment; for SSO the bar is correct splicing plus functional protein
lead: Choose the payload by target cell and compartment first, then fix mechanism, backbone chemistry and readout: both first payloads are splice-switching oligonucleotides, so the gate threshold reads correct splicing ratio plus mature protein, scored on two axes that are never merged.
fig_caption: The five-step RNA pathway, the point at which each payload class acts, the compartments involved, and the qualifying readout per class.
points: Five pathway nodes across two compartments; the dashed line is the nuclear envelope, crossed at export.
Each payload class acts at its own node: siRNA on mature mRNA, gapmer on either side, SSO on nuclear pre-mRNA.
Only the gapmer works in two compartments, which is why its readout needs RNase H1 dependence evidence.
No transport probability or percentage is drawn: the pathway is a framework, not a measured efficiency chain.
CpG/TLR9 sits off the pathway at an endosomal receptor and is scored on a separate set of metrics.
table_note: Backbone chemistry is a third axis: PMO charge-neutral, 2'-modified plus P=S charged
A total-RNA readout is a methodological error for an SSO; occupancy does not cleave
limits: A total-RNA readout is a methodological error for an SSO: occupancy does not cleave the transcript, so any change in total level arises indirectly through splicing and NMD.
CpG/TLR9 endosomal agonism acts at an endosomal receptor, off the RNA pathway, and needs its own metric set; it is never scored together with RNA silencing.
Conjugate PK must be measured on the conjugate: the same antibody clears about four times faster once PMO is loaded.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 §4.2.1, §1, §10.8; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: Payload choice starts from the target cell and the compartment where the drug has to act, and only then fixes mechanism, backbone chemistry and readout. siRNA acts on mature mRNA in the cytoplasm, a gapmer cleaves through RNase H1 in either compartment depending on where the target RNA sits, and an SSO occupies nuclear pre-mRNA without cleaving it. Because both first payloads are SSOs, the receptor-entry & payload-fit gate and the patient-cell biology gate record correct splicing ratio and mature protein on two separate axes and never collapse them into one score. Cut for space: the full mechanism comparison table and the three separate sources behind the DAR and backbone conclusions.

title: Seven steps from systemic dose to clinical benefit; the step still to be proven is productive payload
lead: Each step in the chain needs evidence of its own, and the step no public conjugate programme has shown directly is the fourth: payload arriving in the active intracellular compartment of the target cell. That is what the first study is designed to answer.
fig_caption: Seven-step evidence chain. Solid arrow: routinely measurable. Dashed arrow: the link most often missing today
points: Every step carries its own evidence
Step four is the open question
Three misreadings skip a level
Tissue signal is not cell entry
table_note: Per-step read-outs and the controls each requires are set out in the memo
limits: The chain is a conceptual framework; no measured per-step efficiency is attached to it in the source material.
Of the thirteen priority programmes reviewed, none reports a direct measurement at the productive-payload step.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 (§2.1, Appendix D); data as of 2026-10-13
notes: This is the spine of the whole evaluation. Everything later in the deck — which entry receptor, which payload, which gate releases money — hangs off the claim that step four is the open one. The three misreadings at the bottom are the ones to watch for when a competitor or a partner presents delivery data: tissue fluorescence, homogenate RNA knockdown, and generalising from a single programme to a platform.

title: Crowding sits at the entry and rights layers, not the disease layer
lead: Of 94 disease records, 45% share one receptor family, so the first wave backs the single entry with human PD, TfR1 into skeletal muscle. Differentiation stays in payload sequence and disease use, and the 18 records whose entry is still undiscovered run as a separate receptor-discovery route.
fig_caption: Candidates placed by biological confidence against entry grade; COL6A1 is repositioned, and the four axes are kept apart.
points: 45% of the 94 disease records sit in one receptor family, so crowding is at the entry layer, not the disease layer.
Only GAA IVS1 and DYSF share the platform unit - same TfR1 entry, myofibre nucleus and nuclear splicing.
COL6A1 moves off that circle: its product cell is the interstitial fibroblast nucleus, so its entry needs separate proof.
GAA's slot is already taken at same receptor, target and mechanism by a Creyon 36 nt aptamer; ABX1100 is the comparator.
Four axes are marked on four channels - y, x, symbol, border - and never collapsed into one score.
table_note: Entry families of 94: TfR1/CD98hc 42, local dosing 12, other receptors 10, immune/blood 8
18 records still need their entry receptor discovered - the moat candidate set
limits: The map answers where work is already under way, not where work is worth doing; that second question is answered by the four-axis grading.
The five counting columns use different units and no two may be added; the 26 adjacent-technology records are likewise not additive.
Of the 31 records ready for mechanism validation, 13 are CNS, 6 eye, ear and skin, 3 skeletal muscle and 3 kidney.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 §3.3, §3.4, §4.1.7, §6.1; registry status check 2026-10-11; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: The figure repositions COL6A1 away from GAA IVS1 and DYSF: its product cell is the muscle interstitial fibroblast nucleus, which is not the myofibre nucleus under the platform-unit definition, so it no longer shares a platform unit with the other two. Only GAA IVS1 and DYSF share the large circle. Biology, delivery, competition and resource dependency are marked on four separate channels and are never combined into a single score. title: Five evidence labels say what each candidate still lacks; three axes set the order of work
lead: The three axes are entry feasibility, payload-mechanism maturity, and availability of rights and resources; each is scored separately.

regions.heading: Priority comes from three axes, scored once each
items: On those axes the first cluster is only two candidates, both on TfR1 into the myofibre nucleus: GAA IVS1 and DYSF.
A label reads one axis only, how far disease biology and payload mechanism have come; it carries no entry-feasibility information.
Entry feasibility must therefore be scored on its own; ranking labels high to low as an investment score sets entry risk to zero.
The labels are not summed and are not turned into a score card; eight original labels were standardised into five, with the denominator recomputed to 100%.
Remaining candidates go into three different queues: receptor discovery, failure explanation, or retained control arm.

source: Source: IC Memo v2 §2.5, §6.1, §7.6, §7.8, Appendix A; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: The labels tell us which link each candidate is still missing and what the next experiment should be; they do not rank investments. 'Delivery proof missing' means specifically that productive intracellular payload has never been measured, which is what the receptor-entry & payload-fit gate buys. For the delivery-increment group, the comparator is a three-arm design: same payload, naked payload, and the best alternative route. Cut for space: the mapping from eight original labels to five and the cross-tabulation of the 31 mechanism-validation records by entry grade.

title: Antibody format is derived from target cell and compartment, then fixed by our own same-payload comparison
lead: Format follows from the mature myofibre and the nucleus rather than from a literature ranking, and is settled by a same-payload, same-model comparison we run ourselves. Antibody gain is measured on functional delivery, safety window and durability, and antibody supply gates the start.
fig_caption: Carrier mass plus one loaded siRNA duplex across six binder formats, against the glomerular-filtration magnitude and current AOC use.
points: The smaller the carrier, the larger the share of mass one 13 kDa oligonucleotide duplex takes.
About 60 kDa is a first-approximation filtration level, so Fab and everything below sit near or under it.
Clinical precedent exists at IgG, Fab, Centyrin and peptide mass; scFv has no AOC data this round.
Format follows from the mature myofibre and the nucleus, then from our own same-payload comparison.
Antibody gain is read on functional delivery, safety window and durability - never summed into a score.
table_note: VHH-Fc fusion rises to tens of kDa and is no longer glomerularly filtered
Charge and plasma-protein binding move real clearance off the mass threshold
limits: No same-payload, same-model head-to-head between formats exists in this round's material, so formats are not interchangeable parts.
No sub-rating is merged into an overall delivery score and there is no score card; the three antibody-gain dimensions are also shown separately.
The one read-out to buy sits with WuXi Biologics, so closing antibody supply is a hard precondition for starting the receptor-entry & payload-fit gate.
source: Source: IC Memo v2 §4.1, §4.1.2, §10.8; data as of 2026-10-13
notes: The smaller the carrier, the larger the share of mass one oligonucleotide takes, and about 60 kDa is a first-approximation glomerular-filtration level rather than a prediction: charge and plasma-protein binding move real clearance, and a VHH-Fc fusion rises to tens of kDa and is no longer filtered. Clinical precedent exists at IgG, Fab, Centyrin and peptide-ligand mass; scFv has no AOC data in this round's material and VHH appears only in a preprint. The influence of antibody format on AOC delivery is graded as system-dependent, supported only by valency, affinity and epitope having been compared systematically inside a single study.

title: Nine entries graded on five steps: the atlas screens entries and sets the first read-out to buy
lead: Across the 45 cells the evidence stands at 2 publicly comparable, 19 indirect support, 0 vendor narrative and 24 none. The first-wave skeletal-muscle TfR1 row is the only one with human PD yet still carries four indirect cells, so the first money buys two read-outs on that row.

points: Only 2 of the 45 cells rest on a published head-to-head; 19 are indirect and 24 have no evidence at all.
The skeletal-muscle TfR1 row is the only one with human PD, yet four of its five cells are indirect.
Both comparable cells are whole-tissue read-outs, so neither resolves what reaches the target cell.
First money buys two read-outs on that row: cell-resolved payload, then a same-payload format comparison.
Not more dose and not a second entry - the kidney-cell row is blank across all five steps.
table_note: Three company configurations held in parallel: none ranked, none eliminated this round
Evidence level and clinical maturity are separate scales and are never multiplied
limits: Evidence level and clinical maturity are two different scales: they are not multiplied and not combined into a delivery total.
The grading is this report's own reading of the material (research inference), not a systematic review.
Comparable human receptor copy numbers at the blood-brain barrier are unavailable, and anti-CD98 antibodies do not transit the LAT1 substrate channel.

notes: The common constraint across the organ is that the strongest delivery signal sits in the proximal tubule while the target cells are elsewhere, which is what makes the thick ascending limb the clearest platform gap in the atlas. The proximal tubule is the only segment with a candidate entry, through megalin and KIM1, but its disease value is relatively limited and a ligand may suit better than an antibody. If the kidney does work it has the strongest barrier and the longest timescale of the three configurations, which is why it is preferably advanced as a technology collaboration.
